This game hit me like crack did in the 80s, I used to be religiously into Battlerite before stunlock studios inevitably killed it. This game takes that formula, borrows roguelike elements and turns it into an 8 player insane party game that hits that competitive itch without taking itself too seriously. No matchmaker, no MMR, just lobby hosting where you can meticulously tinker with just about every setting like you're setting up a super smash bros lobby. Want a slower round-to-round brawl? Lower the augment reward per round. Want an insane unbalanced DragonBall Z looking fight? Feed the players all of the augments. It's all up to you. BAP HQ may have caught some lightning in a bottle. Hoping it really takes off cause they can absolutely cook here.

Phenomenal game for completely free! Lots of strategic MOBA/hero shooter combat in a battle royale and roguelike package! It may sound strange, but it really does work! There are tons of characters and stages with unique mechanics to play, and tons of masteries and cosmetics to earn for no money! Plus it's super customizable! I've had games with friends where it's anything from a battle royale, to an MMO raid boss fight! Additionally they have local multiplayer and lan play. Including online servers run on your computer! So even if they game would die (It won't) you can still play it. The only sad thing is that this awesomeness isn't currently being updated, but it still has a great online player presence, and it's pretty well balanced. Plus, as a testament to how fun this is, I made a boardgame of it to play it in person with friends who don't own steam! Overall, it's fun, it's free, why not try it?

BapBap is a great game ruined only by the fact that some people refuse to admit their entire playstyle is one giant, screaming, high-speed skill issue. My friends swear their character isn’t OP. Meanwhile: Someone blinks in their direction → TELEPORT Someone exists within 20 meters → TELEPORT AGAIN A fight starts → THE GREAT WALL TOUR 2025 I’m dead → hit by bullets from a player who teleported so far away he’s basically playing on a different server. But no, apparently it’s my “skill issue” because I can’t duel someone who spends 90% of the match in hyperspace. Imagine playing a fighting game and your entire strategy is: Step 1: Run Step 2: Teleport Step 3: Shoot through walls Step 4: Declare everyone else bad Honestly, their character has so many escape tools it could dodge child support. They always say “He’s not broken bro, you’re just bad.” Yeah, okay — if I had a kit made of four dashes, two teleports, three emergency exits, and a gun that hits through geometry, I’d also pretend it was pure mechanics. The only real skill here is how fast they can mash the “run away” button. World-class cardio, zero combat talent. 10/10 masterclass in coping.

Pretty good game with tons of potential, but unfortunately the developers have abandoned it, and the community has mostly moved on as well. The game is still playable, and you can usually find matches without too much trouble. Just keep in mind that the balance is pretty rough, so most players stick to characters like Chuck and Rocky, with the occasional Eve/Zook/Bishop. The rest of the roster feels noticeably weaker or more situational. Free-for-all matches are most common and still a lot of fun, but they can get repetitive after a while. Overall, it's a fun game that's worth checking out since it's free anyway, but don't expect any future updates or balance changes..

BAPBAP is an unusual entry in the multiplayer arena genre, combining the accessibility of a party game with the mechanics of a roguelike hero brawler. Developed and published by Maison Bap, the game throws away many of the conventions associated with competitive online titles and instead embraces unpredictability at every opportunity. Designed as a free-to-play experience for up to eight players, it focuses less on balance and rankings and more on creating entertaining moments that players can share with friends. The result is a game that feels refreshingly unconcerned with esports aspirations, choosing chaos and creativity as its primary selling points. At the center of the experience is an ever-changing progression system built around randomized upgrades. Throughout a match, players collect powers and modifiers that can drastically reshape their character's capabilities. One round may turn a hero into a poison-spewing menace, while the next encourages a build centered around summoned objects, movement speed, or explosive attacks. This constant stream of possibilities gives BAPBAP strong replay value, as players are encouraged to experiment with combinations rather than settle into a single optimal strategy. The roguelike elements are implemented effectively, ensuring that every session feels distinct without becoming overwhelming for newcomers. The roster itself reflects the game's playful personality. Instead of traditional fantasy warriors or military operatives, players encounter an eclectic collection of heroes ranging from mech-piloting fish to eccentric samurai and sentient food items. Each character brings unique abilities to the battlefield, giving them an identity beyond their visual design. Maison Bap has clearly invested effort into making every combatant memorable, and this commitment to individuality helps the game stand out in a crowded multiplayer market. The absurdity never feels forced; rather, it becomes part of the title's charm and reinforces its commitment to lighthearted entertainment. Combat is fast-paced and rewards quick reactions despite the game's casual appearance. Every attack can be avoided with proper movement and timing, placing emphasis on player skill rather than unavoidable mechanics. Battles quickly escalate as arenas fill with abilities, hazards, and environmental interactions. It is common for matches to descend into spectacular confusion as players scramble to survive amidst explosions, summoned objects, and unexpected power combinations. Yet beneath the spectacle lies a surprisingly refined gameplay loop that rewards positioning, awareness, and adaptability. The maps further enhance this sense of unpredictability. Interactive elements allow players to manipulate the environment in creative ways, from disguising themselves as everyday objects to utilizing heavy machinery and other absurd tools scattered throughout the arenas. Random events and environmental surprises keep players engaged, preventing matches from becoming repetitive. These additions make every battlefield feel dynamic and encourage players to remain flexible rather than relying on established routines. BAPBAP succeeds because it constantly presents players with situations they could not have anticipated at the start of a match. One of the more interesting aspects of the game is its philosophy toward online multiplayer. Unlike many modern titles, BAPBAP does not revolve around ranked progression or aggressive matchmaking systems. Instead, it encourages players to embrace the social side of gaming through custom lobbies and community-driven experiences. This approach may not appeal to everyone, particularly those seeking a highly structured competitive environment, but it aligns perfectly with the game's identity. BAPBAP is at its best when played with friends who are willing to laugh at the occasional imbalance and appreciate the ridiculous situations that naturally emerge. Visually, the game features a bright and colorful art direction that complements its energetic gameplay. Character designs are expressive, animations are lively, and the arenas remain readable even during the busiest moments. Combined with its free-to-play model and approachable mechanics, BAPBAP makes a strong first impression and provides enough depth to maintain player interest over time. While it may not redefine the multiplayer genre, it successfully carves out its own niche by prioritizing fun over competition. Ultimately, BAPBAP is a reminder that multiplayer games do not always need to be meticulously balanced or heavily competitive to succeed. Maison Bap has delivered a title that celebrates experimentation, embraces absurdity, and consistently creates memorable moments. Players looking for a serious ranked experience may want to look elsewhere, but those searching for an entertaining arena game filled with unexpected twists will find plenty to enjoy here. Rating: 8/10
